back: A saturated hydrocarbon with only single bonds, general formula $\ce{C_nH_{2n+2}}$.
They have only strong single C–C and C–H bonds and no functional group.
notes: Their reactions: combustion, and substitution with chlorine in UV light.
Plenty of oxygen; blue flame; most energy released.
Limited oxygen; yellow, sooty flame; soot: CH₄ + O₂ → C + 2H₂O.

back: It is toxic, colourless and odourless, and combines with haemoglobin so the blood carries less oxygen.
notes: Ventilate rooms with braziers, paraffin or gas heaters.

back: A reaction in which one atom or group of atoms is replaced by another.
notes: Methane + chlorine: an H atom is replaced by a Cl atom.

front: Why is the methane–chlorine reaction called photochemical?
back: Ultraviolet light provides the activation energy; there is no reaction in the dark.
notes: Supplement; ZIMSEC also asks about the dark.

front: Order for balancing a combustion equation
back: Carbon first, then hydrogen, then oxygen; double the equation to remove any half.
A yellow, smoky flame and black soot on pots; carbon monoxide may also form.
